outcome: Capability closure now records existing support before request creation
owner_impact: Research AI must now classify every paper/Experiment requirement before creating a capability request. Requirements already expressible by deployed capabilities or the stable Lab contract are stored with machine-readable support evidence and never enter the Professor queue. Only genuinely unsupported requirements can create or reuse candidate requests; scientific ambiguities remain explicit without creating requests. The Already Supported Professor response remains available only as the exceptional cleanup path for a false positive that still slips through.

next.text: No owner action is required. The approved two-ticket capability-request protocol repair is complete and this bounded repair scope is closed. The broader Professor capability-request domain (#58) remains a living product domain with its real queue handled separately.

technical_evidence: Normalized closure requirement rows classify supported, unsupported and ambiguous requirements per append-only analysis.
Supported requirements require machine-readable implemented capability IDs and/or stable contract paths and cannot be referenced by capability requests.
Every unsupported requirement must link to at least one reused/new unavailable candidate; ambiguous requirements must retain an explicit ambiguity and cannot create requests.
Legacy analysis JSON remains readable as an unsupported/ambiguous compatibility projection while v11 resume exposes normalized requirement/support history.
MCP capability-request interface is v11 and server version is 3.18.0; tool count and authoring language remain unchanged.
